item.title: STEVE MOORE: The IRS became judge, jury and executioner in a tax-code witch hunt against Americans
item.description: An aggressive IRS enforcement campaign has swept more than 1,100 syndicated conservation-easement disputes into audits and litigation.
item.content:encoded:
I’m a flat tax guy like Steve Forbes, Chairman & Editor-In-Chief, Forbes Media and author of "Flat Tax Revolution," so in an ideal world, we wouldn’t stuff the IRS tax code with special tax breaks and instead would have one simple, low rate of 18% for everyone.

But if Congress passes tax laws steering people and businesses into certain activities, it can’t just snatch those incentives away indiscriminately. This is called a "bait-and-switch" trap, and here’s a perfect example of such a misdeed.

More than 60 years ago, the IRS created a program called a conservation easement through a revenue ruling. Its goal was to protect nature, stop development, and save working lands. Landowners received a tax incentive for voluntarily setting aside a portion of their land from development. The law has been in effect since 1976 — nearly 50 years. The tax break was made permanent in 1980 and has been part of the tax code ever since.

To further encourage this land preservation policy, individuals, business partnerships, and corporations were permitted to donate to these land easements in exchange for a tax write-off. The result? Tens of millions of acres have been conserved.

IRS RAISES BUSINESS MILEAGE DEDUCTION RATE AMID FUEL PRICE SURGE

Then, in late 2016, IRS officials who disapproved of these syndicated conservation-easement transactions unilaterally changed the rules of the game. Notice 2017-10 did not formally abolish the conservation-easement deduction, but it branded a broad category of transactions as "listed transactions," imposed burdensome disclosure requirements, and opened the door to an aggressive campaign challenging taxpayers who used them.

They retroactively labeled partnerships participating in the program "presumptively abusive."  This aggressive IRS enforcement campaign has swept more than 1,100 syndicated conservation-easement disputes into audits and litigation, including roughly 740 cases docketed in U.S. Tax Court and about 400 transactions still under examination as of May 2026.

The IRS improperly issued Notice 2017-10, branding an entire category of these legal, decades-old transactions presumptively abusive, retroactive to 2010.

No proposed rule. No public comment. No vote by anyone accountable to voters.

Just an IRS notice — followed by an increase to a 100% audit rate for all transactions of this kind. The result was an abusive enforcement campaign that has now clogged the U.S. Tax Court with more than a thousand cases.

TENS OF MILLIONS OF TAXPAYERS MAY BE OWED IRS REFUNDS FROM COVID-ERA

If there are bad actors, of course, they should be punished. A bipartisan Senate Finance Committee investigation identified serious abuses in some syndicated conservation-easement transactions, particularly deals involving inflated land valuations and outsized deductions. But evidence that some promoters abused the deduction does not give the IRS license to presume that every transaction was fraudulent or that every investor knowingly participated in a tax shelter.

By using cookie-cutter metrics and conducting desk audits, the IRS has harassed law-abiding taxpayers, pressured them to pay tens of millions of dollars in unfair "settlement agreements," forced some to file for bankruptcy, and treated them like common criminals despite their having followed the law.

Clearly, the IRS changed tax law after the fact, which is only legal "with respect to criminal and penal cases, but not civil revenue measures." On top of that, the IRS does not make the laws. Congress does. Sadly, the IRS continued this aggressive approach during the Biden administration, when the agency received a major infusion of funding and personnel that expanded its enforcement capacity. Rather than correcting the campaign’s procedural and fairness problems, the administration allowed it to continue against taxpayers caught in these long-running conservation-easement disputes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Perhaps the most ironic part is that the IRS itself was caught engaging in illegal activity.  In a May 2026 report, the Treasury Inspector General found seven cases involving backdated penalty-approval documents; the IRS conceded more than $68 million in penalties in those cases.

Even so, IRS officials have frightening leeway to make allegations of tax fraud, then serve as judge, jury, and executioner, forcing people to pay tax bills that aren’t actually owed. It is a pattern of abuse that Americans have come to recognize: an agency substituting its own policy preferences for the law Congress wrote, then using its enforcement powers to punish law-abiding citizens who relied on the statute as written.

It’s time for Congress to amend tax laws to prohibit after-the-fact tax changes so that trust and fairness in the tax code can be restored.

In addition, the IRS should issue clear guidance on how to make a proper donation of a conservation easement and how to prudently value the deduction without creating later controversy.

Finally, the IRS should immediately end the witch hunt against law-abiding taxpayers who were encouraged by Congress and the Treasury Department for decades to participate in conservation easement programs.

Simply put, this is weaponization at its worst — and it is un-American.

item.title: MIKE SARRAILLE: Extortion 17's heroes died once. America must never let them die twice
item.description: A new Fox Nation special honors the 31 Americans killed when their CH-47 Chinook was struck in Afghanistan's Wardak Province on Aug. 6, 2011.
item.content:encoded:
PROGRAMMING ALERT: The Fox Nation special "Final Flight: The Men of Extortion 17" is available to stream now on Fox Nation.

Fifteen years after Extortion 17 became the deadliest single incident for U.S. forces in the war in Afghanistan — and the greatest loss of life in Naval Special Warfare history — our duty is to ensure the men aboard are never forgotten.

There is an old saying that a soldier dies twice: first, when he draws his final breath; and again, when his name is spoken for the last time.

On Aug. 6, 2011, some of America’s finest warriors died their first death. It is a cliché to say these men were the best of us, but in this case, it is simply true. Gen. "Wild Bill" Donovan, founder of the World War II-era Office of Strategic Services, once described such operators as "Ph.D.s who can win a bar fight" — individuals possessing brilliant, highly specialized intellects while also having the grit to get their hands dirty.

SEAL TEAM 6 MEMBER EXPLAINS BLUNT REALITY OF COMBAT AND EXPECTATIONS IN THE BLACK OPS WORLD

Thirty-one Americans, including Navy SEALs, Air Force special operators and Army aviation soldiers, alongside their Afghan commando counterparts, boarded a CH-47 Chinook helicopter to answer a call for support. The helicopter was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade in Afghanistan’s Wardak province, killing everyone aboard. In an instant, they were gone. But their stories remain.

Extortion 17 is not merely a call sign, a date or an entry in the history of a long war. It was personal. The Navy SEALs aboard that helicopter belonged to SEAL Team 6’s Gold Squadron. I knew these men. They were my brothers-in-arms.

FOREIGN BLACK OPS MEMBER REVEALS THE SECRET AMERICAN UNIT HE LOVED WORKING WITH IN COMBAT

They were among the most elite warriors our nation has ever produced — highly trained men who operated in the shadows, accepted long periods away from their families and carried burdens most Americans will never fully understand.

They were also among the kindest, most empathetic and respectful human beings you could ever meet.

That is the paradox of the American warrior.

These men possessed a rare and necessary ability. They could dim their empathy like flipping a switch, bring overwhelming violence against evil on our behalf and then return home to be dad again. They were the monsters our enemies feared and the fathers, husbands, sons and brothers their families needed.

AS AN ARMY WIDOW, I WILL NEVER FORGET HOW ORDINARY AMERICANS HONORED MY HUSBAND

On that fateful night, Rangers from the 75th Ranger Regiment were engaged with the enemy in the Tangi Valley and needed reinforcements. When the call came, the men of Extortion 17 did not hesitate.

They did not debate the danger. They did not take a vote. They simply flew off into the night.

In doing so, they upheld a covenant few Americans will ever understand: When your brothers are in harm’s way, you go. Even when the risk is extraordinary. Even when death may await you.

That is a warrior’s life.

We are blessed as a nation that such men and women still live among us — the "damn few" willing to carry the burden for the overwhelming majority.

While filming our Fox Nation special "Final Flight: The Men of Extortion 17," commemorating the 15th anniversary of their deaths, I sat down with former teammates, parents, wives and siblings of the fallen. Fifteen years have passed, but the pain remains fresh. The chairs are still empty. The voices are still missed. The holes left behind have never truly been filled.

SIX AMERICAN HEROES EVERYONE SHOULD KNOW THIS MEMORIAL DAY, FROM DELTA FORCE TO A WWII BOMBER CREW

Yet these families have moved forward — not past the loss, but with it. They carry the weight of their loved ones with the same quiet strength those warriors carried for this country. Their sacrifice did not end on Aug. 6, 2011. It continues every morning they wake up and choose to keep going.

America owes them more than a moment of silence once a year.

We owe them remembrance through action. We teach their names. We tell their stories. We teach our children that freedom is not self-sustaining. It demands strength, sacrifice, stewardship and love of country. We remind them that the peace they inherited was purchased by men and women willing to stand between their families and evil.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Remembrance is not passive. It is a duty — a duty to be worthy of their sacrifice. We cannot repay the men of Extortion 17. But we can refuse to let them die twice.

item.title: MORNING GLORY: Rogers versus El-Sayed is a referendum on the future of America
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's narrow Michigan Senate Democratic primary win over Haley Stevens sets up a high-stakes fall battle against GOP nominee Mike Rogers.
item.content:encoded:

In 2024, Rogers — a very respected, former seven-term Congressman from Michigan who served as Chairman of the House Intelligence Committee — tallied 2,693,680 votes, or 48.30% of the total electorate in the state in a Senate race he lost to Elissa Slotkin. Republicans need only turn out the same electorate as voted in 2024 and Rogers will win the 2026 race.

That sort of turnout is usually, however, a big lift in a non-presidential year, because statewide elections are not as exciting to the average American as presidential contests.

That El-Sayed hates the state of Israel is not open for debate. He does. El-Sayed, himself a Muslim, will probably energize the estimated quarter of a million Muslims in the Wolverine State as well as the Jewish population of approximately 120,000 people (about 1.2% of Michigan’s population). Most Jews and many non-Jews believe that El-Sayed is simply antisemitic, and certainly the most extreme mainstream party candidate to ever run for, much less serve in, the United States Senate.

El-Sayed will energize all sorts of demographics within the electorate, but given the polarization that follows in his wake, count on the national media camping across the state from now until November and covering every twist and turn in this campaign.

Count on Republicans across the country, as well as supporters of Israel who are not Republicans from all across the country helping Rogers raise funds for his campaign. His campaign website began to cook even before the El-Sayed primary victory was certain.

item.title: New York gubernatorial candidate urges 9/11 attendees to turn away from Mamdani during ceremony
item.description: Bruce Blakeman says attendees should turn their backs on NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani at the 9/11 memorial over his refusal to condemn "globalize the intifada."
item.content:encoded:
Bruce Blakeman, the Republican candidate in New York's gubernatorial race, said Wednesday that attendees at this year's Sept. 11 memorial ceremony should turn their backs on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani if he attends.

"I would equate this to a wake. You don't go to a wake if you're not welcome," Blakeman, whose nephew was killed in the South Tower on Sept. 11, 2001, and who currently serves as Nassau County executive, told reporters.

"I think it's completely appropriate if family members ask him not to come, but if he does come, I think there's a respectful and peaceful way to protest that and I would suggest that people turn their back on the mayor," he said.

FIREFIGHTER BROTHER OF 9/11 VICTIM INCENSED BY 'RADICAL' MUSLIMS WINNING KEY DEM PRIMARIES

Blakeman argued Mamdani's refusal to condemn the phrase "globalize the intifada" should disqualify him from attending the ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks.

"He's not welcome there because he has yet to say anything in opposition to the global intifada. As a matter of fact, it seems like he supports that phrase, which is part of the reason why we had the tragedy we had on 9/11," Blakeman said.

Mamdani's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

The mayor has said he still plans to attend the ceremony.

9/11 FAMILIES PUSH TO BAN MAMDANI FROM 25TH ANNIVERSARY REMEMBRANCE OVER 'HOSTILE' RECORD

"I will proudly honor the families, the survivors, the first responders forever impacted by that horrific terror attack by standing alongside them at this year's 9/11 commemoration — reaffirming that we will never forget the solemn day..." Mamdani said last week.

His comments came after relatives of Sept. 11 victims launched a petition urging the National September 11 Memorial & Museum to bar Mamdani from attending the ceremony in Lower Manhattan.

"Concerns have been raised about Mr. Mamdani's public positions, associations, and responses to rhetoric that many perceive as hostile to these shared values," the Change.org petition states.

"Given these concerns, we respectfully ask that the organizers carefully consider whether Mr. Mamdani's participation would align with the intention of the ceremony and the expectations of the families most directly affected by the tragedy."

JEWISH LEADERS FAULT MAMDANI RHETORIC AS UPPER WEST SIDE STABBING, HATE CRIME PROBE CONTINUES

A spokesperson for the 9/11 Memorial & Museum previously told Fox News Digital that the organization has "intentionally worked to keep the commemoration free of politics because remembering those we lost on 9/11 should never be a partisan issue."

"Government officials from across the political spectrum, including every sitting president, governor, and mayor since 9/11, have attended the ceremony simply to bear witness — they do not deliver remarks and are asked to remain in a designated area," the spokesperson added.

Former New York Gov. George Pataki was also asked Wednesday whether Mamdani should attend the ceremony.

"It's my nature to be inclusive, and that is my instinct, but Sept. 11 is different. So, I may have comments on that," Pataki said, according to the New York Post.

Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

item.title: Florida man allegedly attacked sister with machete while she was sleeping next to toddler daughter
item.description: A Florida man is facing charges after he allegedly hacked his sleeping sister with a machete as her 1-year-old daughter was lying beside her in the bed.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida man is accused of slashing his sister with a machete while she was sleeping in bed next to her 1-year-old daughter, according to officials.

Ruben Altidore, 36, repeatedly hacked at his sister in her bedroom in an unsuccessful attempt to kill her on Monday in Margate, which is located about 40 miles north of Miami, according to an arrest report per WPLG.

"Oh my God, why aren’t you dead yet?" he shouted during the attack, according to the arrest report.

Altidore was arrested on Monday in connection with the attack. He was charged with attempted felony murder, aggravated child abuse and violation of probation, according to jail records.

BELOVED TEACHER KILLED AS SHE SLEPT, DAUGHTER STABBED IN ATTACK AS MOTIVE REMAINS UNCLEAR: DA

His sister survived the attack but suffered serious injuries.

She suffered a 10-inch wound that reached the bone on the back of her right thigh, a four-inch laceration to the back of her right hand with the possible amputation of at least four fingers, a near amputation of her left index finger and thumb and a cut to her left palm with a near amputation of her left thumb, according to investigators.

The victim’s 1-year-old daughter was found after the attack lying in the bed covered in blood, though investigators said the child was not injured.

The woman eventually managed to escape and ran to a neighbor for help, WPLG reported, adding that her piercing screams were captured on home surveillance video.

MAN FACING FEDERAL CHARGES AFTER ATLANTA TRAIN PASSENGER STABBED ABOUT 20 TIMES, FBI INVESTIGATING

"My [brother] is trying to kill me," the woman reportedly screamed as investigators arrived at the scene, according to the police report.

A cousin of the victim also told investigators that Altidore attacked his sister with a machete, and a neighbor reported hearing the victim screaming after she ran outside following the attack.

"She ran to the middle of the street and then ran to my front door where she was asking for help," neighbor Luis Pereria told WPLG. "Apparently she was sleeping when this all happened. I was just baffled by it. How can you do that?"

Investigators found a large amount of blood inside the victim’s bedroom that was tracked into the hallway, to a bathroom door and outside the home.

A machete sheath was discovered in the kitchen, and a machete was found under a bed with what appeared to be "red smudges," investigators said.

Altidore was taken to the Broward County Main Jail and is being held without bond.

A motive for the attack remains unclear at this time.

item.title: Retired NFL standout Roddy White suggests Ryan Clark's outspokenness may have played role in ESPN exit
item.description: Roddy White questions ESPN's decision as Steve Smith is expected to take an expanded role following Ryan Clark's departure from the network.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN’s latest round of layoffs last week included former NFL players-turned-TV analysts Ryan Clark and Cam Newton, as well as reporter Tom Pelissero, who had joined the company from NFL Network. Clark’s exit drew particular attention after more than a decade with the network.

The moves come as ESPN prepares for one of its most significant NFL coverage seasons yet, a run that will culminate with the network’s first Super Bowl broadcast.

Front Office Sports reported that former All-Pro wide receiver Steve Smith is expected to have an expanded role on ESPN studio programming. ESPN confirmed Monday that Jason McCourty will join "Monday Night Countdown," appearing to step into the opening created by Ryan Clark’s layoff. McCourty joined ESPN in 2024 and is now exclusive to the network after leaving his CBS game analyst role earlier this year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Former NFL wide receiver Roddy White is among the latest sports figures to weigh in. White, who faced Clark during their playing careers, said Clark’s abrupt ESPN exit stood out because of how highly he regarded the former analyst’s work.

"I think Ryan Clark is exceptional at his job," he said. "It's unfortunate that he got released by ESPN because he is so good at what he does. Usually, guys who are that good don't lose their jobs."

White also pointed to Clark’s outspokenness on issues beyond football, suggesting it may have been a factor in the separation.

"Clark speaks up on a lot of issues outside of football. He is always standing up for the Black community and being on our side. I think this, and his opinionated nature, may have cost him his job because ESPN, as a network, doesn't want people touching on politics and community-related topics. They just want everything to be sports-related."

5 OPTIONS TO REPLACE RYAN CLARK ON ESPN'S SUPER BOWL HALFTIME SHOW

White finished his 11-year career with the Atlanta Falcons with 10,863 regular-season receiving yards.

Clark had been one of ESPN’s more visible NFL voices, regularly appearing on "NFL Live," "First Take," "Get Up" and "SportsCenter." In 2023, at the 44th Annual Sports Emmy Awards, he took home the Sports Emmy in the Outstanding Personality/Studio Analyst category for his work across ESPN platforms.

Clark had also been a fixture on the "Countdown" desk alongside Scott Van Pelt since 2023. His layoff, however, drew added scrutiny because it reportedly happened during an "NFL Live" broadcast, prompting questions about how the network handled the move.

In 2021, Clark launched "The Pivot Podcast" with former NFL players Fred Taylor and Channing Crowder. He has also hosted "Inside the NFL" since 2023.

item.title: Trump blasts Democratic socialist candidate as 'full of s---' and Dems are skipping socialism 'for communism'
item.description: Trump singled out Abdul El-Sayed by name during a Las Vegas speech, calling communism the greatest threat facing the U.S. in its history.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump escalated his attacks on Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed Wednesday, singling out the progressive candidate as "full of s---" while arguing Democrats are embracing communism.

The remarks came hours after El-Sayed narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democrat Senate primary, winning by less than one percentage point after The Associated Press called the race early Wednesday.

He will face Republican Mike Rogers in November for the Senate seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters.

Trump devoted several minutes of his Las Vegas speech to attacking democratic socialist candidates, arguing they are advancing communist ideas and calling communism "the greatest threat" facing the United States.

SOCIALIST SURGE: FAR-LEFT DEMOCRATS TEST NATIONAL PLAYBOOK AFTER BLUE-CITY PRIMARY SHOCKS

"These people are dangerous and frankly, they are lunatics. They're crazy, and we can't let them get into office," Trump said. "Communism is the greatest threat to our country in its history, including even World War One, World War Two, Pearl Harbor, 9/11. I think it's the greatest threat."

The White House later amplified that portion of Trump's remarks on social media, posting simply: "Communism is the greatest threat to our country."

Trump mocked what he said communist policies would mean for Americans.

"Would you like a free house? We'll take one from your neighbor. Would you like free rent? We'll take it from whoever. We'll take your building away from the landlord," Trump said. "What they don't say, and what Republicans should say, is that at the end of the year, you'll have nothing but death, squalor, poverty. You'll have a life of hell."

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

The president pointed to Venezuela as an example of what he said happens when communist policies take hold.

"Look at Venezuela, where it was such a rich country 20 years ago," Trump said. "Every time this has happened, you go through squalor ... filth, crime, death, destruction, embarrassment. You lose your home. You lose your apartment."

Trump then singled out El-Sayed by name, drawing one of the loudest reactions of the night.

"When I watch Abdul, he's full of s---," Trump said.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

El-Sayed's victory gives Democrats a progressive nominee in one of the country's most closely watched Senate races. Backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., El-Sayed campaigned on Medicare for All, getting money out of politics and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

He has described himself as a capitalist and has distanced himself from the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), though Republicans have frequently tied him to the broader democratic socialist movement.

Trump later returned to a familiar theme from the second term of his presidency.

"If you remember, during my State of the Union speech, I made a very strong statement. I said that America will never be a socialist country," Trump said. "I was right."

The president argued Democrats now want to move beyond socialism.

TRUMP HAILS AMERICA AS 'MOST EXCEPTIONAL NATION EVER TO EXIST' IN MOUNT RUSHMORE SPEECH

"What I didn't say is what they're trying to do. They want to skip socialism. They want to go right down to the bottom of the barrel. That's communism," Trump said. "They want it to be a communist country. We're not letting them have it as a communist country, not even for a minute."

Trump closed by vowing to defeat what he called the Democrat Party's leftward movement.

"Together we will defeat communism, socialism and Marxism in America once and for all," Trump said. "It's defeated. It's going to go down. It always goes down."

The White House and El-Sayed's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Fox News Digital's Andrew Mark Miller, Kiera McDonald, and Robert Schmad contributed to this reporting.

item.title: Crowded Russian beach descends into chaos after alleged Ukrainian drone incident kills 7, including 4 children
item.description: A projectile struck a crowded Russian Black Sea beach Monday, killing seven people, including four children, and injuring 58. Russia blamed a Ukrainian drone attack as video captured the deadly impact.
item.content:encoded:
Vacationers were sent scrambling for safety Monday after a projectile struck a crowded beach in a Russian Black Sea resort town, killing seven people, including four children, and injuring dozens more, officials said.

Video footage captured the incident in the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik, where the beach was packed with visitors at the time of the strike.

The Russian Mission in Geneva said in a post on X that the "bloody attack" was carried out by a drone launched by Ukraine, accusing Kyiv of targeting civilians.

UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

"The attack targeted civilian infrastructure. Emergency and special services are working at the crash site," regional Gov. Veniamin Kondratyev said in a post on Telegram.

"What happened today is a targeted attack by the Kyiv regime against civilians who have no connection to the military infrastructure. This cynical and inhumane terrorist attack against children cannot be justified." 

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

Andriy Kovalenko, an officer with Ukraine’s Defense Forces, disputed Russia’s account, saying the deaths were directly caused by Russian air defenses that intercepted a drone, sending debris onto the beach.

"Russian air defense shot down a drone over people lying on the beach," Kovalenko said on Telegram.

In the video, sounds resembling gunfire were heard just seconds before a drone struck the beach, causing a fireball explosion that sent bystanders screaming. As the gunfire was heard, the drone appeared to veer sharply before diving toward the beach.

Preliminary Russian reports also found that several of the deaths were caused by "falling drone debris," Kondratyev said.

ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR

In another Telegram post, Kovalenko indicated that Ukraine uses its weapons against Russian military-industrial infrastructure to affect Moscow’s ability to finance the war.

item.title: Florida man accused of cutting off diver's air supply in fight over coveted lobster diving spot
item.description: A dispute over a lobster diving spot during Florida's lobster mini season allegedly turned deadly when a man shut off a diver's surface supplied air.
item.content:encoded:
A battle over a lobster diving spot off the Florida coast allegedly escalated into an underwater nightmare after a man was accused of shutting off another diver's air supply, a confrontation that landed him behind bars on an attempted murder charge.

Michael Joseph Simpson, 51, surrendered Tuesday to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center in Miami-Dade County, where he was booked Tuesday evening on an attempted murder charge, according to Miami-Dade jail records. His bond was set at $10,000.

According to Local 10 News, the incident occurred shortly after 7 a.m. on July 29 about a half-mile east of Fisher Island during Florida's annual lobster mini season.

Citing the arrest affidavit, Law&Crime reported that Simpson allegedly approached another boat at a high rate of speed and circled the vessel several times before anchoring about 10 feet away.

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE

Investigators say the confrontation began after Simpson claimed the group was diving in "his spot" and warned that a larger boat was on its way before it arrived and anchored nearby.

Authorities allege Simpson then threatened to turn off the surface-supplied air system providing oxygen to an 18-year-old diver searching for lobsters. Investigators say Simpson jumped into the water and intentionally shut off the unit.

As the confrontation unfolded, witnesses yelled, "We have a diver down there you a--hole!" according to the arrest affidavit cited by Law&Crime.

The diver's boat owner jumped into the water and pulled him to the surface. The diver was gasping for air and appeared disoriented but was not injured, Local 10 reported.

FLORIDA MAN GIVES AN INCREDIBLE INTERVIEW ABOUT HOW HE FOUGHT OFF AN ALLIGATOR WITH A FISHING POLE

Investigators allege Simpson left before deputies arrived. After authorities identified him as the suspect, Simpson voluntarily surrendered Tuesday, according to Local 10.

Simpson's attorney, Howard Srebnick, strongly denied the allegations in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing investigators ignored evidence and witnesses he says support his client's account.

Srebnick said Simpson was diving from his own boat with friends and his two young children and "never disabled anyone's diving equipment."

Srebnick said video shows one of the accusers becoming entangled in the Brownie's Third Lung air system while Simpson "was nowhere near it."

AMERICAN TOURIST ATTACKED BY SHARK IN VACATION HOT SPOT

He also disputed investigators' allegation that Simpson fled, saying his client instead idled his boat away from the immediate area to avoid escalating the confrontation before cooperating with responding Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers and providing a statement.

Srebnick said numerous eyewitnesses aboard two separate boats corroborated Simpson's version of events and criticized the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office for arresting his client before interviewing what he described as exculpatory witnesses.

"We are optimistic that the State Attorney's Office, after reviewing the video and interviewing all the eyewitnesses, will dismiss the charges, clear his name, and restore the reputation he has spent a lifetime building," Srebnick said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office for additional comment.

item.title: Bodycam video shows Canadian woman allegedly giving false name before deputies discovered 12 fake IDs
item.description: Body camera video shows Florida deputies finding 12 fake IDs in a Canadian woman's car after she allegedly gave a false name during a traffic stop.
item.content:encoded:
Police body camera video shows the moments Florida deputies arrested a Canadian woman after she allegedly gave a false name during a traffic stop and investigators discovered 12 fraudulent identification cards in her vehicle.

Hillsborough County Sheriff Chad Chronister released the July 29 bodycam footage showing deputies stopping a vehicle in Tampa because its taillights and tag lights were not working.

The driver, Bryce Swanson, 28, initially identified herself as "Brianna Valenzuela" and initially told deputies she had a driver's license but did not have it with her, according to authorities.

SEMITRUCK DRIVER IN DEADLY INTERSTATE CRASH FRAUDULENTLY OBTAINED LICENSE, CITIZENSHIP: OFFICIALS

"Swanson told deputies she did not have an ID and had never possessed a valid driver's license, after initially claiming she did," Chronister wrote on X. "A search of her vehicle revealed 12 driver's licenses with her picture, but different names and dates of birth."

According to authorities, Swanson is a Canadian national who overstayed her visa.

The body camera footage shows a deputy questioning Swanson about her identity after she said she was visiting Florida from New York in a rental vehicle.

"I live in New York," Swanson said. "I'm here in Florida literally just visiting friends and stuff right now."

VIRAL BODYCAM CAPTURES FLORIDA DEPUTY'S TRAFFIC STOP UNRAVEL AS HE ACCUSES ONE-HANDED DRIVER OF HOLDING PHONE

The deputy pointed out she did not have any New York identification.

"Your story's not making a lot of sense to me, right?" the deputy said. "You say you live in New York, but you don't have any ID in New York."

When the deputy again asked how she could live in New York without any identification, Swanson replied, "I've never had a driver's license or anything like that."

Deputies then searched the vehicle and found what investigators described as numerous fraudulent identification cards.

MAN FLEEING ICE OFFICERS IN FLORIDA IS STRUCK AND KILLED BY TRACTOR-TRAILER, POLICE SAY

"All these are fake," one deputy said in the video before placing Swanson under arrest.

Swanson was booked into the Orient Road Jail and charged with driving without a valid driver's license and providing a false name to a law enforcement officer.

She is being held without bond because of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainer, according to jail records.

Fox News Digital has reached out to ICE for comment.

item.title: Federal judge acknowledges Supreme Court ruling clearing path for Trump to end Haiti TPS
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that the court order blocking Trump's termination of Haiti TPS is no longer in effect after the Supreme Court's ruling.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday notched a major immigration victory after a federal judge acknowledged that the court order blocking the administration from ending temporary protected status (TPS) for hundreds of thousands of Haitians is no longer in effect after the Supreme Court's ruling in Mullin v. Doe.

The ruling marks the culmination of a yearslong legal battle over the Biden administration's expansion of Haiti's TPS designation and delivers a significant immigration victory for Trump, who repeatedly campaigned on ending the Biden administration's expanded TPS protections for Haitians.

The issue became a centerpiece of the 2024 election after Trump and running mate JD Vance blamed the Biden administration's Haiti TPS policies for the influx of Haitian migrants into Springfield, Ohio, where residents raised concerns about traffic safety, strained public services and cultural clashes.

BLUE STATE LEADERS ERUPT AFTER SUPREME COURT’S DECISION ENDING TPS PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIANS, SYRIANS

The controversy later exploded onto the national stage after Trump referenced residents' claims that migrants were taking ducks and geese from parks and eating household pets.

The White House did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment by publication time.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes wrote Wednesday that her earlier order staying the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) termination of Haiti's TPS designation "is no longer in effect" after the Supreme Court's decision and the D.C. Circuit's subsequent mandate.

While the underlying lawsuit will continue, the administration is no longer barred by the injunction from moving forward with ending TPS protections for an estimated 330,000 to 350,000 Haitians living in the U.S. 

The remaining litigation centers on whether the administration acted with unconstitutional racial animus in terminating the designation.

LIBERAL COURT STUNS WITH RULING THAT HANDS TRUMP MAJOR IMMIGRATION WIN

The Supreme Court ruled in June that the TPS statute bars judicial review of the administration's non-constitutional decisions to terminate TPS designations and found the plaintiffs' equal protection challenge was unlikely to succeed. The court reversed the lower courts and remanded the case for further proceedings.

DHS General Counsel James Percival pushed back on reports suggesting Wednesday's order itself ended Haiti's TPS designation, arguing the protections effectively expired when the Supreme Court's mandate was issued July 27 and that Reyes' order merely acknowledged that legal reality.

"Haiti TPS ended when the Supreme Court mandate issued on July 27," Percival wrote on X. "I will give Judge Reyes kudos though for taking the L with grace and not doing something bonkers like many of her colleagues."

Haiti first received TPS after the country's devastating 2010 earthquake, but the designation remained in place for 16 years through multiple administrations. The Biden administration later expanded and extended protections for hundreds of thousands of Haitians already living in the U.S.

MORE THAN 100 HAITIAN IMMIGRANTS WITH VIOLENT OFFENSE AND SEX CRIME CONVICTIONS DEPORTED: DHS

After reviewing conditions in Haiti, former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem determined the country no longer met the statutory requirements for TPS and announced the administration's decision to terminate the designation, arguing the humanitarian program had been extended well beyond its intended temporary purpose. The move triggered the legal challenge that ultimately reached the Supreme Court.

After the SCOTUS decision, the DHS announced Haiti's TPS designation would be terminated, effective July 27, and that employment authorization documents issued under the designation were no longer valid. The department instructed employers to reverify the work authorization of affected employees.

The State Department maintains a Level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory for Haiti because of widespread gang violence, kidnappings and civil unrest.

Fox News Digital's Danielle Wallace and Michael Lee contributed to this report.

item.title: Dodgers ruin baseball with sixth straight loss, get swept for second consecutive series by Chicago Cubs
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have lost six straight games after the Tarik Skubal trade, and their once-insurmountable 14-game lead continues to shrink.
item.content:encoded:
Discussion on baseball-related social media over the last week has focused on one topic, and one topic only: the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Dodgers, back-to-back World Series champions, entered the weekend leading up to the Major League Baseball trade deadline with several major question marks, despite their massive payroll. Starter Blake Snell remained injured, with just three innings pitched in 2026 after only 61 innings in 2025. Tyler Glasnow was also sidelined with a back injury after throwing only 39.2 innings earlier in the season. Emmett Sheehan, after a breakout 2025, had struggled mightily in recent starts, and the injuries had forced LA to turn to journeyman Eric Lauer.

So they did what any team trying to win a World Series should do, and made their roster better. Instead of hoping for the best, LA's front office traded Zyhir Hope, River Ryan, and Brady Smith to the Tigers for defending AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. This set off a firestorm of anger, outrage, hatred, and conspiracy theories, as well as wailing and gnashing of teeth from commentators and fans who demanded that owners lock players out to pocket more money, or acted as though this marked the end of baseball.

LOS ANGELES DODGERS TRADE FOR TARIK SKUBAL HIGHLIGHTS MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL'S MASSIVE PROBLEM

Why? Because the Dodgers were now simply too good to be beaten. No team could compete with their combination of talent and depth. The season, and postseason, were effectively over.

And as if part of some divine plan, the Dodgers chose this very week to demonstrate to fans, those commentators, and the "ruining baseball" casuals why they're all hopelessly wrong. LA hosted the Red Sox at Dodger Stadium late last week, and were promptly swept by a surging Boston team. They allowed six straight runs in the late innings of game one to lose 9-4, managed just two runs on 10 hits in a 3-2 loss in game two, then gave up four home runs in game three to lost 8-4.

After that loss, they flew to Chicago to face the Cubs, another team on a hot streak in recent weeks. After jumping out to a 3-0 first inning lead in game one, starter Justin Wrobleski gave up four home runs, leading to a 10-5 blowout loss.

Skubal made his Dodgers debut on Tuesday afternoon, going six innings and allowing just two runs with six strikeouts. The Dodgers lost 5-1, with just a solo home run from Kyle Tucker to show from their vaunted, unbeatable offense.

TARIK SKUBAL'S DODGERS DEBUT ENDS IN DECISIVE 5-1 LOSS TO CUBS AS LA DROPS FIFTH STRAIGHT GAME

Then, on Wednesday, the Dodgers got a leadoff home run from Shohei Ohtani and proceeded to allow seven straight runs to the Chicago offense. Two homers from Pete Crow-Armstrong and a parade of hits from the bottom of the Cubs lineup made it 7-1 heading into the eighth inning. The Dodgers, to their credit, displayed a modicum of fight, putting up five runs in the inning, but came up short in a 7-6 loss.

Six straight losses. Just two wins in their last eight games. LA also fell to 8-13 in their last 21 games, and has yet to win in August. The best case scenario would be a win on Friday, meaning they'd have gone more than a week without a win. Should the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the San Diego Padres later Wednesday evening, their once insurmountable 14-game lead over second place will drop to eight games. Ahead of a weekend series between the Diamondbacks and Dodgers in Phoenix.

Over their last six games, the unbeatable LA juggernaut has been outscored 42-22 by the opposition. While they once had a stranglehold on the first overall seed in the National League and the first round bye, they're now several games behind the Milwaukee Brewers and could fall behind the Atlanta Braves into the third seed, should Atlanta hold their lead against the Miami Marlins.

Which means that were the season to end today, the Dodgers would be playing in a wild card series. Ruining baseball indeed.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Again, this is the problem with that talking point. Are the Dodgers better than the Cubs or Red Sox? Sure, probably. But over the course of an entire season, 162 games, the gap in winning percentage between those teams might be as little as 5%. Meanwhile, in the NFL, the Patriots and Seahawks won 82.4% of their games in 2025. The Chiefs won 88% of their games in 2024. The gap between teams in baseball, despite the lack of a salary cap, is much smaller than in most other sports. Which is why the best team frequently wins the Super Bowl, and doesn't always, or even often, win the World Series in baseball.

Instead of acknowledging this, the Skubal trade has given rise to conspiracy theories from Brewers fans that the Tigers took the Dodgers offer because of some type of hypothetical collusion. Or something. Even though the Tigers wanted MLB-ready controllable starting pitching, which the Dodgers offered, and the Brewers reportedly didn't. It's given rise to many within and outside baseball demanding a salary cap, which will have little impact on the outcome of the games, but a tremendous impact on the ability of owners to pocket more profits.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

And it's made many ignore that for all their talent, the Dodgers have plenty of flaws too. Kyle Tucker has been a tremendous disappointment, having the worst offensive season of his career. Mookie Betts has been a well-below-average hitter this year. Edwin Diaz has allowed nine runs in 8.2 innings. Yes, Snell and Glasnow are expected to return soon, but are frequently injured and no guarantee to stay healthy. Roki Sasaki has been wildly inconsistent. Their bullpen has been among baseball's worst for the past month.

Does this mean LA won't win the World Series? No. But it does demonstrate that nothing in baseball is a foregone conclusion. That there's no way to predict outcomes in a postseason series in August. And that acting as though LA is unbeatable or ruining baseball is as wrong and delusional as believing owners care about the "health" of the game or anything but higher profits.

item.title: Halle Berry sizzles in racy lingerie look for sunset beach stroll during Fiji getaway
item.description: Halle Berry shared stunning Fiji vacation photos in a gold bikini and animal-print cover-up as she prepares to celebrate her 60th birthday soon.
item.content:encoded:
Halle Berry is enjoying a tropical reset ahead of her 60th birthday.

The 59-year-old actress shared a series of Instagram photos from a tropical getaway in Fiji, offering glimpses of quiet mornings, poolside relaxation and sunset walks along the beach.

Berry posed near the shoreline in an animal-print cover-up layered over a black lace lingerie bodysuit as the sun dipped toward the ocean. 

The flowing black-and-white wrap featured wide sleeves and tassel detailing, while her short, tousled hair blew across her face as she smiled for the camera.

KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION

"The only bad thing about this trip is that each day must come to an end," she captioned the post.

A separate Instagram post captured the Academy Award winner in silhouette beneath sheer fabric draped around an outdoor daybed. Berry arched backward as the setting sun streamed through the material, with palm trees, an infinity pool and the ocean visible beyond the shaded retreat.

In a separate poolside image, the "Catwoman" star reclined along the edge of the water in a gold bikini. A wide-brimmed straw hat rested across her torso as she stretched one arm across the wooden deck and displayed several rings and stacked bracelets.

Berry also shared an artful reflection photographed through a glass window. The layered image showed the actress appearing to relax inside a rounded bathtub while the surrounding ocean, palm trees and outdoor pool reflected across the glass.

GISELE BÜNDCHEN CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY IN LEOPARD-PRINT BIKINI AS SHE REFLECTS ON GRATITUDE

The actress appeared to be enjoying the laid-back pace of the trip, joking in another caption, "We got drunk last night, and still drunk today 🤪."

Berry’s vacation comes as she prepares to celebrate her 60th birthday and continues challenging expectations about how women should approach aging.

During a July appearance on Hoda Kotb’s "Making Space" podcast, Berry said the milestone feels far different than she once imagined.

"I’m so happy to still be here, you know. When I was growing up and I thought of 60, it felt so old, you know. And now that I am 60, um, it doesn’t feel old at all," she said. "You know, I’m like, this is 60. Well, that’s not so bad."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Berry said she feels more comfortable and confident in herself than she has in years.

"I feel really great actually. If I’m honest, I feel, I think, better than I have in a very, very long time," she said. "Um, I feel more of myself. I feel all of myself."

The Oscar winner explained that growing older has allowed her to stop worrying about satisfying everyone else’s expectations.

"You do stop managing everybody’s expectations," Berry told Kotb. "You do start to realize you’re usually the oldest person in the room. And, so, with that, you know, that carries some weight. You get to do what you wanna do.

'KNOTS LANDING' ICON DONNA MILLS JOINS ONLYFANS AT 85 TO CONNECT WITH FANS 'ON HER OWN TERMS’

"You get to be who you wanna be, say what you want to say. You know, you’re no longer walking on eggshells, and that’s a really wonderful place to arrive."

Berry also pushed back against the idea that reaching a certain age should mean stepping away from her career permanently.

The actress said people have asked whether she intends to continue making movies before suggesting she has already accomplished enough.

"'Are you still going to keep working in movies?'" Berry recalled being asked. "And I say, ‘Yeah, why should I not?’"

She said others have questioned whether it is time for her to "quit all that and sit down somewhere and just be on a permanent vacation."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Berry rejected the assumption that women should withdraw from professional life as they grow older, arguing that meaningful work continues to provide purpose and connection.

"Why do I wanna? After I’ve worked my whole life so hard and it’s made me feel all of myself, it’s validated who I was, it’s, it’s given me a sense of purpose," she said. "Why should I now sit down and give that all away? And then what?"

The actress said she encourages her 18-year-old daughter, Nahla, to pursue work she genuinely loves so that retirement never feels like the ultimate goal.

"Choose what you love so that you never feel like you want to retire because working and being active and contributing is what keeps us young as we go down the path of life," Berry said.

"It keeps us connected to life, to ourselves, to the others. You, you never want to stop doing that thing that you love so much."

item.title: Masked man caught on camera smashing Virgin Mary statue with a hammer outside NYC church
item.description: Surveillance video shows a masked man climbing a fence and smashing a Virgin Mary statue with a hammer at St. Rita Church in Long Island City.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Police Department (NYPD) is investigating the destruction of a Virgin Mary statue outside St. Rita Roman Catholic Church in Long Island City as a possible hate crime after a man climbed over a fence and repeatedly smashed it down using a hammer.

In surveillance video released by the Diocese of Brooklyn, the masked man violently hits the statue outside the church in what Catholic officials say is the latest in a string of attacks targeting the parish.

In a press release, church officials said it is the fourth reported vandalism incident targeting the parish since 2024, and the New York City Police Department is investigating the latest vandalism as a possible hate crime.

ANCIENT ESTATE TIED TO GROUP IN THE BIBLE UNEARTHED WITH 'FASCINATING' TREASURES IN ISRAEL

According to the Diocese of Brooklyn, the incident happened at around 1:42 a.m. Aug. 1.

The video shows the man, who is wearing a dark T-shirt and shorts, climb over the fence into a courtyard where a statue of the Blessed Mother stood.

The suspect removes a hammer from his pocket and repeatedly strikes the statue before knocking it off its pedestal. He then climbs back over the fence and walks away.

The Diocese said in a statement the attack was the fourth vandalism incident at St. Rita Roman Catholic Church since 2024.

WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY BEHEADING JESUS STATUE OUTSIDE CATHOLIC CHURCH

Past acts of vandalism at the parish include the destruction of a 60-year-old stained-glass window and graffiti that defaced a statue of St. Francis of Assisi and the sidewalk.

There was also damage done to a statue of St. Jude inside the church.

The Diocese of Brooklyn told Fox News Digital no arrests had been made.

"This week, the NYPD also issued a crime stats update and hate crimes are up by 9.4% over the same 7-month period (Jan-July) of last year," John Quaglione, deputy press secretary for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Brooklyn said.

item.title: Amazon driver caught on video flinging customer’s package onto porch in infuriating delivery blunder
item.description: Ring camera video shows a Yun Express driver hurling an Amazon package onto a Florida porch, snapping a proof-of-delivery photo and walking away.
item.content:encoded:
A delivery driver is under scrutiny after a doorbell camera captured a package sailing through the air instead of being carefully delivered.

Ring camera video shared by Florida resident Nathan Pekas shows the driver approaching the home, hurling a package onto the concrete porch, raising a handheld device to take a proof-of-delivery photo and then walking away as a dog howls from inside the house.

The box lands with a loud thud in the video before the driver snaps the photo and leaves without placing the package at the front door.

Pekas told Storyful the package was delivered by Yun Express, a third-party carrier used for some Amazon deliveries.

TEXAS DOORDASH DRIVER GETS HIT BY A CAR FLEEING FROM POLICE AND STILL DELIVERS THE ORDER

He also shared a photo showing what appeared to be damage to one corner of the box.

The Florida resident said he was surprised by the driver's handling of the delivery, joking that the state's sweltering summer heat "must have been too much to make those extra two steps to the door."

Amazon acknowledged the incident in a statement provided to Storyful.

DOORDASH DRIVER HAILS KEY TRUMP POLICY AFTER DELIVERING MCDONALD'S TO WHITE HOUSE: 'I'M GOING TO ENJOY IT'

"This video does not reflect the standards we have for our delivery partners, and we're looking into this matter," an Amazon spokesperson said.

It was not immediately clear whether the contents of the package were damaged or whether the driver remains assigned to make Amazon deliveries.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Amazon for additional comment.

The incident is the latest package delivery to go viral after being captured on a homeowner's doorbell camera.

Last month, a FedEx driver in Georgia made headlines after tumbling backward into a front yard swimming pool while stepping away to take a proof-of-delivery photo.

The driver quickly laughed off the mishap, joking, "I needed that," before climbing out of the pool and returning to the delivery route.

"If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it," she added, referring to the spread of smallpox that killed many Indigenous Americans.

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

"I’m a chef, and one of the first meals that I made that was for the community when I was 16 [years old] was a Thanksgiving meal," Hong said. "I always think my hospitality background in owning a restaurant for seven, eight years, that bringing folks around the table to share conversation and build community is always a good thing.

"But Thanksgiving is also a time that’s incredibly painful for many people in our communities," Hong continued. "And, so, I think there, I wanted to make sure that people understood that there are multiple views, but views can evolve.

"And the position that I'm running for right now, and I think my background as a chef will actually help me become a better governor that's able to bring more people to the table."

LEFT’S LATEST SOCIALIST DARLING DRAGGED OVER ‘WHITENESS’ COMMENTS PULLING IN HER OWN FAMILY: ‘WEIRDO RACISM’

Fox News Digital reached out to Hong's campaign for comment.

Republican Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany criticized Hong's original posts on Fox News Tuesday, accusing her and other socialist candidates of wanting to "destroy" American culture.

"Well, considering she also posted, ‘Please DON'T gather for the colonizer holiday,’ and just days ago called Thanksgiving ‘incredibly painful,’ it's hard to believe she now claims it's her favorite holiday. But this goes far beyond Thanksgiving. It's part of the broader socialist message that seeks to tear down the traditions, institutions, and values that bring Americans together," Tiffany said. 

"Whether it's Thanksgiving, Christmas, Culver's, the police or even Valentine's Day, Francesca Hong has spent her entire political career criticizing the very fabric of Wisconsin and the traditions that bring our communities together."

item.title: El-Sayed's threat against GOP rival backfires as conservatives bring receipts: 'Is Dubai in Florida?'
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's "safe quarter" remark directed at Mike Rogers after winning the Michigan Senate Democratic nomination sparks heated online debate.
item.content:encoded:
Abdul El-Sayed sparked online controversy moments after capturing the Democratic Party’s nomination in Michigan's Senate race for his word choice in challenging Republican nominee Mike Rogers to a series of five debates.

"I know you're going to say no because you're a coward. Five debates. All right?" El-Sayed said.

"You and I both know that you will wither in front of your own crimes, but I'm gonna make sure Michiganders know about them. By the time we're done, you are not going to have safe quarter from people holding you accountable for what you've done," El-Sayed continued.

The language of "safe quarter" is raising eyebrows among viewers online.

The online backlash demonstrates how closely the Michigan Senate race is being watched across the country and how viewers are analyzing every move of El-Sayed in particular.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

The former local public health official succeeded in his race against Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., a more establishment candidate with the backing of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., despite being heavily outspent.

His campaign has been a proxy for larger questions in the Democratic Party of whether the progressive label and promises of aggressively expanded public sector involvement will resonate with its base over the relative safety of establishment messaging.

But it has also invited scrutiny.

Conservatives ripped El-Sayed on social media for attacking Rogers' out-of-state vacation home while he owned multiple rental properties overseas. Doug Powers, a longtime editor and contributor for Twitchy, believes it clashes with El-Sayed's financial disclosures revealing that he owns property not just out of the state but also overseas.

"If I’m the Rogers campaign, I’m putting this in an ad. ‘A socialist who owns property in Dubai and India is attacking me for having a vacation house in Florida while threatening me in my home state?’" Powers wrote in his own post to social media.

"’No safe quarter from people holding you accountable’ is commie messaging," he added.

"The easy rebuttal for Mike Rogers here is to point out that El-Sayed owns property in a luxury development in Dubai," Chuck Ross, an investigative reporter for The Washington Free Beacon, pointed out.

"Is Dubai in Florida?" yet another account wrote.

Fox News Digital previously reported that El-Sayed's most recent financial disclosure exposes how El-Sayed and his wife own at least two foreign properties in Bangalore, India and Dubai. The Dubai property is worth up to $250,000.

Other conservatives slammed El-Sayed for the tone of his message and suggested it was putting a target on the back of his Republican rival.

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

Scott Jennings, the conservative political personality and media commentator on CNN, bashed El-Sayed's phrasing at the victory press conference.

"Abdul el Sayed threatening the safety of his opponent while the Jewish Democrat AG of Michigan says she can't go to a Dem convention because she's not safe, either. Does everyone see what's happening here?" Jennings wrote in a post to X, referring to recent developments in the Wolverine state over anti-Semitic comments.

Brian Newberry, a Rhode Island state representative and former minority leader, echoed Jenning's concern.

"Democratic U.S. Senate nominee, who pals around with [a] guy who celebrates 9/11, tells his Republican opponent that he will ‘not have safe quarter’ in his home state. Who the hell does this guy think he is?" Newberry wrote, hinting at El-Sayed's association with Hasan Piker, a progressive streamer who has drawn backlash for past comments of his own.

"And will any — and I mean ANY — Democrat condemn this rhetoric?"

AG Hamilton, a popular conservative X account, called on El-Sayed to bring more clarity to the statement.

"Someone should ask el Sayed what exactly this means because it certainly comes off as a threat of political violence aimed at his opponent," the account wrote. 

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the phrasing or on whether the online reactions were overblown.

DEMS SELECT THEIR CANDIDATE TO FACE LONGTIME GOP LAWMAKER WHO BALKED AT VIRGINIA REDISTRICTING

In his remarks on Wednesday morning, El-Sayed continued to press his case against Rogers.

"Mike Rogers is a guy whose politics and vision and perspective are old. Mike Rogers is a guy who has never shied away from a corporation he could do a favor for," El-Sayed said.

"If you want a senator who’s going to lick some boots, fine. Go vote for Mike Rogers. But if you want a senator who’s going to stand up to Donald Trump, then you’ve got your option right here."

With the Democratic primary in the rearview mirror, El-Sayed will face off against Rogers in the state’s general election Nov. 3.

item.title: Taxpayer-funded housing for illegal immigrants in GOP's crosshairs: 'It's got to stop'
item.description: Sen. Bill Hagerty's bill would require citizenship verification for public housing and block sanctuary cities from Community Development Block Grants.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., is introducing new legislation that works to restrict illegal aliens from reaping federal housing benefits, blocking loopholes and cutting off access for sanctuary cities to receive federal community development grants.

"[Illegal immigrants] have been allowed to participate in federally subsidized housing programs," Hagerty told Fox News Digital. "They're using American taxpayer dollars to jump to the front of the line while putting Americans at the back of the lines. It's got to stop."

The End Housing Welfare for Illegal Aliens Act is part of a larger effort by both the Trump administration and GOP members of Congress to halt illegal immigrants and sanctuary cities' ability to thrive, which they claim often comes at the expense of benefits for the American people.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

"The Trump administration has taken a look at this," Hagerty said. "The preliminary estimates are 24,000 of these illegals are utilizing HUD programs. Again, crowding out Americans that would be deserving of these programs and, again, putting illegals into these positions."

The bill Hagerty is putting forward codifies the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) efforts to close loopholes that allow illegal immigrants to receive federal benefits on taxpayer-funded housing if they are roommates with eligible individuals.

"HUD housing assistance is intended for U.S. citizens and certain eligible noncitizens, yet HUD resources serve only a quarter of eligible households in need," HUD said in a statement. "Meanwhile, a recent HUD and DHS audit of all assisted households identified nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown eligibility verification. Furthermore, HUD estimates approximately 24,000 illegal aliens, ineligibles and fraudsters in 20,000 ‘mixed status households’ benefit from HUD assistance."

Hagerty’s bill, if passed, would enforce this proposed rule by HUD Secretary Scott Turner under all administrations.

"This current administration is going to do everything it can, I'm certain, to stop this type of fraudulent behavior," Hagerty said. "But what I want to do is preclude this from happening if there were ever to be another Democrat administration."

GOP SENATORS RALLY AROUND NEW DHS PROPOSAL TARGETING SANCTUARY CITIES: 'SHOULD PAY A PRICE'

Hagerty also said the legislation would eliminate Biden-era incentives for sanctuary cities by denying these cities access to Community Development Block Grants (CBDG), federal funding that supports affordable housing, infrastructure and local services.

He also argued that, under the Biden administration, the adoption of sanctuary city policies was incentivized because those lacking citizenship documentation are still included in population counts when considering congressional representation.

"What the Biden administration did, they were creating incentives for people to come here illegally," Hagerty said. "You think about where they situated sanctuary cities — in blue states, where they're losing population, where they’re losing voters."

"Why?" Hagerty said. "Because you can count these illegal aliens for the purpose of allocating congressional districts. You can count them for the purpose of locating electoral votes. That is the motive behind the crime."

'AMERICA FIRST' IMMIGRATION OVERHAUL BILL WOULD CODIFY TRUMP'S CAMPAIGN PROMISES ONCE AND FOR ALL

The bill would require public housing authorities to verify citizenship before providing housing assistance. This would change the law so agencies "shall" verify citizenship, meaning they are legally required to do so, instead of saying they only "may" do so.

It would also specifically bar illegal immigrants from being eligible for both Section 202 and Section 811, which provide affordable housing for low-income elderly and people with disabilities.

"Illegal aliens are pushing out and crowding out people that are disabled, American taxpayers that are disabled, elderly that are disabled," Hagerty said.

Hagerty’s efforts to crack down on any negligence in restricting illegal immigrants from federal programs comes amid a broader fight by the Trump administration and Republicans in Congress to crack down on illegal immigration throughout the country.

"The goal is to pass the legislation," Hagerty said. "And I think if you polled Americans, you'd find this is extraordinarily popular."

item.title: Explosive drone forces shutdown at major German airport serving NATO, Ukraine flights
item.description: An explosive-armed drone was found near a Ukrainian plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport, prompting Germany's interior minister to warn of a hybrid attack.
item.content:encoded:
A drone carrying explosives was found near a Ukrainian plane at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport late Tuesday, prompting officials to warn the incident represented "a new quality of danger," authorities said Wednesday.

The discovery temporarily shut down both runways at the major European freight hub and forced several flights to divert to other airports, according to The Associated Press.

Another flying object was spotted nearby shortly before midnight and several flights, including one passenger plane, were then diverted to other airports.

JETBLUE FLIGHT REPORTS DRONE STRIKE DURING APPROACH TO NEW YORK AIRPORT: FAA

German police launched a large response and opened an investigation into the two incidents.

Police said an airport worker found the first explosive drone near the airport's south runway with "an unknown explosive device."

An explosives disposal robot was deployed to examine the device before authorities removed its detonator.

The plane, bearing the blue and yellow colors of the Ukrainian flag, displayed the English-language slogan, "Be Brave Like Kherson," a tribute to the southern Ukrainian region, Deutsche Welle reported.

In the second incident, an unidentified flying object collided with a cargo aircraft that had aborted its landing at Leipzig/Halle Airport because of the runway closure.

HELICOPTER REPORTS NEAR MISS WITH RC PLANE NEAR JFK AFTER JETBLUE DRONE STRIKE

The aircraft diverted to Hannover Airport, about 125 miles north-west of Leipzig, where officials found minor damage, according to The Associated Press.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the discovery of the first drone marked a significant escalation.

"Drone sightings, drone threats, including in a hybrid context, are something we know from the past," he said. "That a drone armed with explosives is at an airport is a new threat scenario."

Dobrindt also described the incident as "a hybrid attack scenario."

He said questions about the type of explosives used, the drone's origin and who was responsible remained under investigation.

"All the speculation that is currently going on about the explosives, the construction, the question of the drone, the origin and, of course, who is behind it, is now part of the investigation," Dobrindt said.

"What is happening now also shows that the assessment made months ago — that we are dealing with a high level of danger — was justified."

In June, Dobrindt opened Germany's Joint Centre for Countering Hybrid Threats, which brings together federal and state security agencies to address threats including espionage, sabotage and disinformation.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

Leipzig/Halle Airport is a major European cargo hub, and Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft are based there.

NATO said it was aware of the incidents but referred questions to German authorities.

RUSSIA LINKED TO ARSON ATTACKS ON PROPERTIES CONNECTED TO UK PM KEIR STARMER, POLICE SAY

Ukraine's ambassador to Germany, Oleksii Makeiev, suggested Moscow may have been behind the incident, telling Welt TV Wednesday, "Who else could it be but Russia?" according to reports.

In 2024, an incendiary device ignited at a logistics center at Leipzig/Halle Airport, setting fire to a freight container in an incident Western security officials suspect was part of a Russian intelligence sabotage operation.

item.title: In Nevada speech, Trump chases after toddler on stage before joking he doesn't want him to 'be Biden and fall'
item.description: Trump invited a Las Vegas casino waitress and police officer's family on stage, where their toddler delivered a Trump Account thank-you.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump shared a pair of lighthearted moments with a toddler during a Nevada event Wednesday, first stepping in to stop the young boy from wandering off-stage before joking, "I don't want him to be [former President Joe] Biden and fall off the stage."

The moment unfolded after Trump invited Sandra and Brad, a Las Vegas couple, on stage at the Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa with their two young children as he touted his administration's Trump Accounts and "no tax on tips" initiatives.

'PAWN STARS' ICON RICK HARRISON SAYS TRUMP TAX POLICIES CHANGE EVERYTHING FOR SMALL BUSINESSES

DEMOCRATIC MARYLAND GOV WES MOORE PRAISES TRUMP ACCOUNTS AS ‘SMART POLICY’

"Thank you for my Trump Account," the little boy repeated into the microphone, prompting an uproar of applause from the crowd.

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid has a blunt response to everyone freaking out over Travis Kelce's dad bod
item.description: Andy Reid insists Travis Kelce came back in good shape, but practice footage and declining 2025 stats tell a different story for fantasy football owners.
item.content:encoded:
NFL training camp is barely a week old, and the Kansas City Chiefs already find themselves embroiled in a full-blown investigation: Has Travis Kelce succumbed to the dreaded dad bod?

The internet's amateur body-fat analysts went to work last week after pictures of a noticeably thicker Kelce made the rounds.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid wasted little time trying to put out the fat fires Wednesday, telling the media his star tight end is bigger but allegedly in good shape.

FANS STUNNED AT TRAVIS KELCE'S TRAINING CAMP PHYSIQUE AFTER NUPTIALS TO TAYLOR SWIFT

"He came back in good shape," Reid insisted.

"I know everybody's out there saying he's got the dad body and all this stuff, but he looks the same to me that he's always looked, and [he's] playing like crazy." Reid even claimed the veteran is "focused in and ready to go" for every practice snap.

Kelce is officially listed at 250 pounds, but if you apply the eyeball test to the practice footage, that scale might be doing some heavy lifting.

The guy is 36 years old, which is basically 50 in tight end years.

TAYLOR SWIFT MARRIES TRAVIS KELCE

Kelce spent the offseason pounding beers in VIP suites on the Eras Tour, married Taylor Swift in July, and expanded his media empire. He has three Super Bowl rings, infinite money, and a life on easy mode, even if he remembers his six-pack abs all too well.

With all that in mind, you'd be forgiven for wondering why he's still doing this. So why are we dragging this out?

Look at the numbers from last season. In 2025, Kelce posted a modest 76 catches for 851 yards and five touchdowns. For normal mortals, those are decent numbers. For Travis Kelce? That is a clear slide down the hill.

Father Time remains undefeated, and carrying extra offseason weight certainly isn't going to turn back the clock.

HALL OF FAMER CRIS CARTER SAYS UPCOMING NFL SEASON WILL BE TRAVIS KELCE’S ‘LAST DANCE’

Which brings us to the real conspiracy: why is someone in your fantasy league still going to reach for him in the early rounds?

Don't let it be you.

Every August, fantasy owners convince themselves a declining superstar is somehow about to turn back the clock.

Then by Week 4, they're wondering why they burned a premium pick on yesterday's highlights instead of tomorrow's breakout.

Draft upside players, not household names living off past glory. Let someone else chase the nostalgia and pray for one last vintage season.
